points.text: Google's September 2026 spam update started on 24 Sep and can take up to two weeks to roll out. Log traffic changes against that window and hold off on big content changes until it ends. Google hasn't said which spam types it targets, so don't diagnose drops yet.

AI referrals convert well but are tiny. Orbit's 29M-visit dataset shows AI visitors are 3x more likely to become leads, yet AI is only 0.5% of traffic. This is medium confidence, and AI traffic is undercounted because AI Overviews and AI Mode land in Organic Search. Track AI referrals as a high-intent channel, but don't move budget away from organic search. Semrush's manufacturing study adds that mentions, citations and referral traffic don't move together, so measure them separately.

Single-run AI visibility numbers are unreliable. Orbit's sample is very small (three brands, low confidence) and found the four LLMs almost never cited the same domain. Profound's persona tests were consumer-only and medium confidence, but they also showed answers shifting a lot. Use repeated runs across engines, and test your key prompts with buyer role context, before trusting any score.

Pages cited by 5+ engines are 5.5 times likelier to hold at week eight
Claude citations are 2.8 times likelier than ChatGPT's to last eight weeks

method.conflict: Yes. Profound sells Citation Decay tracking, which this finding promotes.
method.caveat: Most decay is one-off bursts, measured by Profound's own metric with a 14-day smoothing window.

brief.why_it_matters: Plan a steady publishing cadence, aim for citations across many engines, and track each engine separately.

briefs.title: 69% of Marketers Are Publishing More AI Content Than Last Year (New Research Report)

brief.headline: 69% of surveyed marketers publish a bigger share of AI content than a year ago; 93% use AI.
key_stats: 85% of AI users say they produce content faster; 2.5% say slower
Only 2.7% trust AI content with no human review
7% publish mostly pure AI content, up from 4% in 2025

method.conflict: Yes. Ahrefs sells an AI marketing platform (Letaido) and promotes it in the article.
method.caveat: Small, self-reported sample with unexplained recruitment; smaller than last year's, so year-on-year comparisons are rough.

brief.why_it_matters: Use it as a rough benchmark: AI is standard, but most teams still review output by hand.

briefs.title: Announcing web multimodal Search performance reporting in Search Console  |  Google Search Central Blog  |  Google for Developers

brief.headline: Google added a "multimodal" filter to Search Console for image-based searches like Lens and Circle to Search.
key_stats: Covers Lens, Circle to Search on Android, image uploads, and Chrome right-click "Search this image"
Filter shows in the Search results report and the Generative AI features report
Rolls out globally from September 24, 2026; data can be exported

method.conflict: Google runs Search and Search Console, but this update sells nothing.
method.caveat: No traffic numbers, metric definitions or past data details. B2B SaaS sites may see little image-search traffic.

brief.why_it_matters: You can now see traffic from image-started searches. Check the filter for your site before you spend on visual content.

briefs.title: Has Google demoted listicles?
briefs.unreadable: page has almost no readable text (likely built with JavaScript)

briefs.title: ChatGPT Ads expands across Europe

brief.headline: OpenAI is rolling out ChatGPT Ads to 31 European markets, with self-service now live in Ads Manager.
key_stats: Ads expand to 31 European markets, OpenAI's largest rollout so far
Only Free and Go users see ads; Plus, Pro, Enterprise stay ad-free
Tens of thousands of marketers have already advertised on ChatGPT

method.conflict: Yes. OpenAI sells the ads, and its claim that ads don't affect answers is unverified.
method.caveat: No results, pricing, ad formats or targeting details, so it can't show if ads work for B2B SaaS.

brief.why_it_matters: You can now test paid ChatGPT ads in Europe. Organic GEO work still can't buy answers, since OpenAI says ads don't shape them.

briefs.title: Do Answer Engines customize responses to different personas?

brief.headline: Different personas asking the same AI prompt shared about 1 in 4 brand mentions, versus about 2 in 5 for repeat runs.
key_stats: Cited domain overlap: 34% for the same persona, 20% across different personas
High-income personas got 7.5 brand mentions and 4.8 citations; low-income got 5.8 and 4.1
Clothing queries for people in their 50s and 70s were about 39 points more likely to contain "women"

method.conflict: Yes. Profound sells AI visibility tracking and pitches persona-level tracking.
method.caveat: Consumer topics only, blunt "I am [attribute]" prompts, two weeks, no significance tests.

brief.why_it_matters: One overall AI visibility score can hide gaps for your buyer. Test key prompts with role and budget added.

briefs.title: AI search & manufacturing SEO: What the data shows [Study]

brief.headline: Google AI Overviews covered 57% of tracked manufacturing search volume in July 2026, up from 38% in January.
key_stats: AI Overviews share of search volume: 38% in January 2026, 57% in July, across 458 keywords
AI tools and assistants sent just 0.48% of all sessions to manufacturing sites
Only two domains, Vevor and Grainger, made both the top 15 most-mentioned and top 15 most-cited lists

method.conflict: Yes. Semrush sells AI visibility tools, though the promotion is mild.
method.caveat: Keywords came from Semrush's own rankings, and the authors call results directional, not firm.

brief.why_it_matters: It's manufacturing data, so use it as a rough guide. Track AI mentions, citations and referral traffic separately.

briefs.title: AI chatbots talked 57.5% of AI users out of buying

brief.headline: 57.5% of AI users say a chatbot talked them out of buying something, per a survey of 2,338 US adults.
key_stats: 57.51% of AI users bought a product on an AI tip; 57.5% skipped a purchase because of chatbot info
74.15% of all consumers would be at least somewhat less likely to buy if a chatbot flagged mixed or negative reviews
23.12% would think worse of a product after an AI chatbot ad; 20.36% would think better

method.conflict: Yes. Semrush ends by promoting its own GEO tools, Enterprise AIO and AI Visibility Toolkit.
method.caveat: People self-reported, they were general consumers not B2B buyers, and many stats use small subgroups.

brief.why_it_matters: Chatbots can kill a sale by repeating bad reviews about your brand. Check what they say now. AI ads may not suit B2B.

briefs.title: ChatGPT 5.6 has transformed Shopping mode

brief.headline: ChatGPT Shopping switched from web search to product feeds on July 10th, jumping from 8.26% to 61.54% in a day.
key_stats: Feed-based answers rose from 8.26% to 61.54% on July 10th
Top 10 merchants' share rose from 22.5% to 41.8%; unique merchants fell from 13,524 to 10,607
Shopify is about 35% of feed-based answers; one model explains 83% of swings in 517 customers

method.conflict: Yes. Profound sells Shopping tracking, and its advice to join feeds fits that.
method.caveat: GPT 5.6 is blamed only because of timing, and customers were picked for big swings.

brief.why_it_matters: Matters mostly for physical products. For B2B SaaS, it shows how fast AI tools can change their sources.

briefs.title: Study: AI Declined to Answer Prompts About Our Brand 31% of the Time (But Got Our Info Mostly Right When It Answered)

brief.headline: Across six AI tools, Seer's brand answers were right 95.9% of the time, but AI declined 31.2% of prompts.
key_stats: Wrong answers averaged 2.8%. No-answer rate averaged 31.2%. Total accuracy was 66%.
Comparison prompts: 18.8% accurate, 80.3% no answer. Direct prompts: 90.4% accurate.
Claude was 98% accurate when it answered, but gave no answer 46.3% of the time.

method.conflict: Yes. Seer sells AI visibility services and ends with a pitch for them.
method.caveat: It covers one agency's brand, and Seer doesn't explain how it scored accuracy.

brief.why_it_matters: AI staying silent hurts more than AI being wrong. Comparison prompts got no answer 80.3% of the time, so build outside coverage.

briefs.title: Analysis: Reddit Appears in 83.9% of Google's Discussions and Forums Results

brief.headline: Reddit appears in 83.9% of Google's "Discussions and forums" results worldwide; Reddit, Facebook and Quora hold 76.75% of links.
key_stats: Feature shows in 16.93M of 145M US results (11.7%); Reddit is in 87.8%
After Reddit: Facebook 38.3%, Quora 32%, JustAnswer 8.2%, Mayo Clinic 3.3%
98.7% of appearances are informational intent; 43.2% are for queries of 5+ words

method.sample: 145M US Google results; worldwide size not disclosed
method.data_source: Ahrefs' own SERP and keyword data
method.conflict: Partly. Ahrefs sells Keywords Explorer and Brand Radar, but this finding doesn't need them.
method.caveat: Vendor data with no method given; Reddit's share appears as 83.9%, 84.71% and 87.8%.

brief.why_it_matters: The feature shows in about 1 in 9 US results. Join Reddit, Facebook and Quora; don't build your own forum.

briefs.title: Claude and Claude Code are distinct Answer Engines

brief.headline: Claude Code searched the web in 13% of answers; Claude did in 93%, and they named the same brands 20% of the time.
key_stats: Claude Code searched in 13% of responses vs 93% for Claude; brand overlap averaged 20%
Nearly three-quarters of Claude Code agent visits hit docs, informational and pricing pages, vs 5% for Claude's agent
60% of Claude agent visits hit robots.txt, sitemaps and home pages, vs 4% for Claude Code's agent

method.data_source: Their own prompt runs and tracked domains
method.conflict: Yes. Profound sells AI visibility tracking, and this supports tracking Claude Code separately.
method.caveat: Visit data covers only Profound's undescribed tracked sites, and an AI model labeled the page types.

brief.why_it_matters: If developers buy your product, Claude Code may read your docs and pricing pages. Keep them current and track it separately from Claude.

briefs.title: Where do inaccurate AI claims come from?

brief.headline: Pricing and billing were 12% of AI claims checked but 24% of the wrong ones.
key_stats: Next biggest topic, eligibility and terms, was 4% of wrong claims
51% of brands had a wrong claim citing press or reviews; 54% had one citing their own content
Wrong-claim rates by AI tool run 4.3-6.8%; Claude is over 1.3 times more wrong than ChatGPT

method.sample: 158,000+ AI claims; brand count not disclosed
method.conflict: Yes. Profound sells FactCheck, and this research promotes it.
method.caveat: It's the vendor's new tool, and it doesn't say how claims were checked or how many brands.

brief.why_it_matters: Check your pricing and billing details first, on your site and on outside pages. Treat this as a lead to test.

briefs.title: AI Citations Aren't Your Top KPI: ChatGPT-5.6 Luna Runs More Targeted Searches

brief.headline: ChatGPT's GPT-5.6 Luna used site: searches in 76% of its extra queries, up from 21.6% on GPT-5.5.
key_stats: site: searches (limited to one website): 554 of 729 queries (76%) for Luna vs 158 of 733 (21.6%) for GPT-5.5
Consulted sources fell 43%, from 6,134 to 3,481; open searches fell from 575 to 175
Inline citations fell 12.9%, from 2,054 to 1,790, across 346 matched prompts

method.conflict: Yes. Seer sells AI search consulting, and its advice to track the full process helps that.
method.caveat: One snapshot, small sample, no repeat runs; the reasons given for the shift are guesses.

brief.why_it_matters: If your citations dropped after the model switch, the platform may be why. Note the switch in reports and track site: searches for your domain.

briefs.title: Incident details | Google Search Status Dashboard

brief.headline: Google began rolling out its September 2026 spam update on 24 Sep, worldwide, in all languages.
key_stats: Released 24 Sep 2026, 09:15 PDT
Applies globally and to all languages
Rollout may take up to two weeks

method.timeframe: From 24 Sep 2026; up to two weeks
method.conflict: No. Google runs the search engine but sells no SEO product tied to this.
method.caveat: Google gives only the date, scope and timing, not which spam tactics it targets.

brief.why_it_matters: Expect ranking swings into early October. Log traffic changes by date, hold big content changes, and review Google's spam policies.

briefs.title: AI Overviews Cut CTR by 23.1% in France

brief.headline: French sites where over 20% of queries trigger AI Overviews lost 23.1% of median click rate in nine days.
key_stats: Highly exposed sites: median CTR (click rate) fell 23.1%; 82.2% of them lost CTR
Slope of -0.9 across 963 domains: about one point of CTR lost per point of exposure
All sites: median CTR fell 5.7%; 48% lost over 10% of daily clicks

method.data_source: Google Search Console plus Ahrefs AI Overview rates
method.timeframe: 28 days before vs 9 days after July 22, 2026
method.conflict: Ahrefs sells AI Overview tracking tools, but this finding doesn't directly sell them.
method.caveat: Only nine days of after-launch data, top-click sites only, and not a controlled test.

brief.why_it_matters: Check what share of your queries show AI Overviews, and expect a similar CTR drop. Track clicks and CTR, not impressions.

briefs.title: 2026 Blogging Statistics: Blogger Data Shows Trends and Insights Into Blogging

brief.headline: Only 13.9% of 1,042 bloggers report strong results, an all-time low, even though 92.4% use AI.
key_stats: 13.9% report strong results, down from 20–30% for 12 years. 18% don't know.
92.4% use AI. AI users and non-users are equally likely to report strong results.
Using six or more of eight tactics makes strong results nearly three times as likely.

method.conflict: Yes. Orbit is a content agency that sells a book and similar services.
method.caveat: Self-reported and only shows links, not cause; "strong results" is undefined.

brief.why_it_matters: AI alone won't give you an edge. Keep the hard tactics, like original research and expert input, and track pipeline, not traffic.

briefs.title: LLM Citation Study: 13,184 Citations Across 4 AI Tools | Orbit Media Studios

brief.headline: Four AI tools agreed on a cited domain only 30 times in 1,792 cases (1.7%).
key_stats: 10% to 30% of cited domains also ranked in Google's top 10
Rerun two days later: Claude kept 30% of URLs, Perplexity 65%
Mentioned vs cited: Claude 70% vs 40%, ChatGPT 56% vs 47%

method.conflict: Author sells AI visibility audits, tracks his own site, and has Semrush as a client.
method.caveat: Only three brands and 72 prompts; the author calls it "directional, not statistical proof."

brief.why_it_matters: Don't judge AI visibility from one run or one tool. Track mentions and citations over several weeks.

briefs.title: AI Traffic Conversion Rates: New Research from 97 B2B Websites and 29M visits | Orbit Media Studios

brief.headline: AI-referred visitors convert to leads 3x more than other organic visitors, yet make up just 0.5% of traffic.
key_stats: AI visitors convert 3x more; the typical site sees a 7x gap
ChatGPT converts 2.1% of visitors to leads; Google Search converts 0.5%
AI sources sent 140,000 of 29 million visits

method.conflict: Publisher is an agency that sells AI-readiness and content services, and the article ends with a sales pitch. The finding supports the case for optimizing for AI.
method.caveat: Conversion tiering was manual and the authors call it the most judgment-dependent step. Sites need at least 100 AI sessions, and how the accounts were chosen isn't disclosed. AI traffic is undercounted because AI Overviews and AI Mode land in Organic Search and app visits land in Direct. The reasons given for the gap are hypotheses, not tested.

brief.why_it_matters: AI referrals are worth tracking and optimizing for as a high-intent channel, but at 0.5% of traffic and 100x less volume than Google, they don't replace organic search for lead volume.

briefs.title: AI assistants judge your company by its name - Peec AI

brief.headline: On GPT 5.6 Terra, one in twelve brand descriptions used the name's dictionary meaning, mostly for unknown brands.
key_stats: Live data: a name one point more positive gets described 0.07 points more positively.
Lab: Terra's effect was about four times Gemma's. Gemini's result was not significant.
Well-known brands like Discord, Riot and Slack were unaffected.

method.sample: 904 real brands, 5 assistants; 80 fictional name pairs
method.data_source: Their own Brand Perception data plus lab test
method.timeframe: One week live; lab dates not disclosed
method.conflict: Yes. Peec AI sells AI search tracking, and its own feature produced the live data.
method.caveat: Real-world effect is small; lab used fictional brands and four models; the "unknown brands" reason is untested.

brief.why_it_matters: If your name is a loaded English word and AI doesn't know you, check how it describes you. Build recognition before renaming.

briefs.title: Brand Visibility | ChatGPT and Google AI Approaches by Industry

brief.headline: ChatGPT and Google AI Mode name different brands most often in healthcare (62%) and least in finance (39%).
key_stats: Different brand answers: healthcare 62%, B2B tech 47%, education 45%, finance 39%
Comparison prompts: both agree, e.g. AWS and Azure for cloud platforms
Action prompts: ChatGPT names tools like Kubernetes; Google links tutorials and Stack Overflow

method.sample: Thousands of prompts; exact count not disclosed
method.data_source: BrightEdge AI Catalyst, their own tool
method.conflict: Yes. BrightEdge sells AI Catalyst, the tool behind this data.
method.caveat: "Divergence" is never defined, and the report is gated, so the numbers can't be checked.

brief.why_it_matters: ChatGPT may lean on tool names, Google AI Mode on guides. Cover product and how-to content, but treat it as a hint.

briefs.title: AI Search Visits Surging in 2025—But Organic Search Remains the Cornerstone of Digital Growth

brief.headline: BrightEdge: AI search sends under 1% of referral traffic, while organic search still drives most conversions.
key_stats: AI search is less than 1% of referral traffic
Grok grew 1279% in July; Claude grew 58% in July, 21% in August
34% of AI citations come from PR and media; nearly 10% from social sites like LinkedIn and Reddit

method.sample: Thousands of queries; exact counts not disclosed
method.conflict: Yes. BrightEdge sells enterprise SEO and AI search tools.
method.caveat: Summary of a gated report; no sample sizes or conversion figures, and growth starts from tiny bases.

brief.why_it_matters: Keep investing in SEO basics. Treat AI referrals as early-funnel, and try earning mentions on media and forum sites.

briefs.title: The AI Agent and AEO Organizational Readiness Gap

brief.headline: BrightEdge surveyed over 1,000 enterprise marketers on AI agent and AEO readiness, but shares no results.
key_stats: More than 1,000 enterprise digital and search marketers surveyed
Says most talks with IT and security stall or get blocked (no figure given)
Says teams need more than strategy (no figure given)

method.data_source: Their own survey; recruitment not disclosed
method.conflict: Yes. BrightEdge sells an SEO and AEO platform, and this gated report brings in leads.
method.caveat: Only a gated teaser is public, with no numbers or method, so claims can't be checked.

brief.why_it_matters: Nothing to act on yet. The teaser hints that IT and security talks stall, but shows no data.
